messages.content:
You are an expert synthetic chemist planning experiments to maximise reaction yield.
Each experiment chooses one option for every variable listed. You will see the results
of experiments already run. Choose the next batch to find the highest-yield conditions
in as few experiments as possible. Use chemical knowledge (ligand and base effects,
substrate reactivity, solvent effects) and the observed results. Balance exploiting
good regions with testing informative new combinations. Never repeat an experiment.
Return JSON only.

Pd-catalysed direct C-H arylation of an imidazole to form 5-(2-fluorophenyl)-1-methyl-1H-imidazole-4-carbonitrile (Shields et al., Nature 2021, reaction 3); choose the base, ligand, solvent, concentration and temperature.

Variables and options:
base:
B1: cesium pivalate [SMILES O=C([O-])C(C)(C)C.[Cs+]]
B2: potassium pivalate [SMILES O=C([O-])C(C)(C)C.[K+]]
B3: cesium acetate [SMILES O=C([O-])C.[Cs+]]
B4: potassium acetate [SMILES O=C([O-])C.[K+]]

ligand:
L1: PPhtBu2 [SMILES CC(C)(C)P(C1=CC=CC=C1)C(C)(C)C]
L2: BrettPhos [SMILES CC(C)C1=CC(C(C)C)=C(C(C(C)C)=C1)C2=C(P(C3CCCCC3)C4CCCCC4)C(OC)=CC=C2OC]
L3: X-Phos [SMILES CC(C1=C(C2=CC=CC=C2P(C3CCCCC3)C4CCCCC4)C(C(C)C)=CC(C(C)C)=C1)C]
L4: GorlosPhos HBF4 [SMILES CC(OC1=C(P(C2CCCCC2)C3CCCCC3)C(OC(C)C)=CC=C1)C]
L5: tBPh-CPhos [SMILES CN(C)C1=CC=CC(N(C)C)=C1C2=CC=CC=C2P(C(C)(C)C)C3=CC=CC=C3]
L6: PPhMe2 [SMILES CP(C)C1=CC=CC=C1]
L7: PPh2Me [SMILES CP(C1=CC=CC=C1)C2=CC=CC=C2]
L8: CgMe-PPh [SMILES C[C@]1(O2)O[C@](C[C@]2(C)P3C4=CC=CC=C4)(C)O[C@]3(C)C1]
L9: JackiePhos [SMILES FC(F)(F)C1=CC(P(C2=C(C3=C(C(C)C)C=C(C(C)C)C=C3C(C)C)C(OC)=CC=C2OC)C4=CC(C(F)(F)F)=CC(C(F)(F)F)=C4)=CC(C(F)(F)F)=C1]
L10: PPh3 [SMILES P(C1=CC=CC=C1)(C2=CC=CC=C2)C3=CC=CC=C3]
L11: P(fur)3 [SMILES P(C1=CC=CO1)(C2=CC=CO2)C3=CC=CO3]
L12: PCy3 HBF4 [SMILES P(C1CCCCC1)(C2CCCCC2)C3CCCCC3]

solvent:
S1: N,N-dimethylacetamide [SMILES CC(N(C)C)=O]
S2: p-xylene [SMILES CC1=CC=C(C)C=C1]
S3: butyronitrile [SMILES CCCC#N]
S4: n-butyl acetate [SMILES CCCCOC(C)=O]

concentration:
C1: 0.057 M
C2: 0.1 M
C3: 0.153 M

temperature:
T1: 90 °C
T2: 105 °C
T3: 120 °C

picks.reason: Test whether p-xylene can match the near-quantitative result in butyronitrile under the best base, ligand, concentration, and temperature.
Evaluate n-butyl acetate as an alternative solvent while retaining the established high-yield conditions otherwise.
Check whether the p-xylene solvent response remains favorable at 105 °C.
Measure the temperature sensitivity of n-butyl acetate near the established optimum.
DMAc gave 99.2% at 120 °C, so this tests whether slightly lower temperature preserves its strong performance.
Probe whether DMAc can maintain high yield at 90 °C despite the temperature dependence seen in butyronitrile.
Determine whether the lower concentration penalty observed in butyronitrile also applies in DMAc.
Map the concentration and temperature response in DMAc around its near-quantitative result.
Test whether the lowest concentration is detrimental in DMAc at the highest temperature.
Assess the combined effect of low concentration and intermediate temperature in DMAc.
Complete the untested low-concentration, low-temperature corner of the butyronitrile response surface.
Benchmark PPhtBu2 under the optimal reaction conditions to distinguish ligand effects from the previously tested conditions.
Test BrettPhos under the established optimum to see whether a bulky biaryl phosphine can rival L8.
Evaluate X-Phos at the best-known conditions as a direct comparison with the highly effective L8.
Assess GorlosPhos under the optimal conditions rather than its previously poor, non-matched test.
Screen tBPh-CPhos at the established optimum to test whether its distinct donor properties improve arylation.
Compare JackiePhos with L8 under identical conditions to identify any alternative high-performing ligand.
Test triphenylphosphine under the optimized conditions as a simple-ligand benchmark.
Evaluate P(fur)3 under the optimized conditions to determine whether its distinct phosphine donor characteristics are beneficial.
Benchmark PCy3 under the optimal conditions to separate ligand performance from its earlier low-yield test conditions.
